target_in_paper: Question 7.6 in §7.3 (“Distortion elements and conjugacy classes of elements”): the converse of Proposition 7.5, i.e. whether the non-spreading condition implies distortion for elements of Homeo0(Σ).
correct_elements: Your draft is correctly aimed at a converse question, and in fact the paper itself states Question 7.6 exactly as “Is the converse true?” immediately after Proposition 7.5.
missing_details: You must identify which implication is being reversed: Proposition 7.5 says that if f is distorted in Homeo0(Σ), then lim_{n→∞} diameter(tilde f^n(D))/n = 0.
The ambient group must be specified: Homeo0(Σ), the identity component of the group of homeomorphisms of the oriented surface Σ.
The surface hypothesis from the section must be included: Σ is an oriented surface of genus at least 1.
The universal-cover setup is needed: π: Σ̃ → Σ, a fundamental domain D ⊂ Σ̃ for the deck action, and a compatible metric on Σ lifted to a deck-invariant metric on Σ̃.
The lift tilde f must be specified; implicitly this is the lift used in Proposition 7.5, i.e. the lift associated to an isotopy from the identity / the lift commuting with deck transformations.
If you use the term “non-spreading,” you must define it as the condition lim_{n→∞} diameter(tilde f^n(D))/n = 0.

The meaning of “distorted” must be made explicit, since Homeo0(Σ) is not presented as finitely generated: f is distorted if it lies in some finitely generated subgroup in which the word length of f^n grows sublinearly.
The exact limit expression must be written out; otherwise “the converse” is not stand-alone.
The nearby sufficient condition lim_{n→∞} d_n log d_n / n = 0 (with d_n = diameter(tilde f^n(D))) is context, not the question itself, so it should not replace the target problem.

The reduced follow-up Question 7.7 about conjugates near a rotation or the identity should not be substituted for Question 7.6 unless one explicitly says it is only a reduction discussed after the main question.
refined_question: Let Σ be an oriented surface of genus at least 1, let Homeo0(Σ) denote the identity component of its homeomorphism group, let π: Σ̃ → Σ be the universal cover, choose a fundamental domain D ⊂ Σ̃ for the deck action and a deck-invariant lift of a compatible metric on Σ, and for f ∈ Homeo0(Σ) let tilde f be the lift of f associated to an isotopy from the identity (equivalently, the lift commuting with deck transformations). If lim_{n→∞} diameter(tilde f^n(D))/n = 0, must f be a distorted element of Homeo0(Σ), i.e. must there exist a finitely generated subgroup H ≤ Homeo0(Σ) containing f such that the word length of f^n in H is o(n)?
justification: This is the exact target because §7.3 first defines distortion, then sets up Homeo0(Σ), the universal cover, the fundamental domain D, and the lifted metric, and Proposition 7.5 states the implication “distorted ⇒ lim diameter(tilde f^n(D))/n = 0.” Immediately after that, Question 7.6 asks verbatim, “Is the converse true?” So the intended sharp stand-alone formulation is precisely whether every non-spreading element of Homeo0(Σ) is distorted. The paragraph following Question 7.6 introduces d_n = diameter(tilde f^n(D)), records the stronger sufficient condition lim d_n log d_n / n = 0, and then reduces the problem to Question 7.7, confirming that Question 7.6 itself is the converse of Proposition 7.5 and not a broader neighboring problem.
